summary: Independent verification of src/spine/units.py, src/spine/derive.py, src/spine/assemble.py, src/spine/compose.py and docs/03_WIRING.md, working from HEAD (2e8a63e) plus the uncommitted spine/doc edits, with no report from the agent that made them. Suite is green on every check: ownership 12+18, contract 14+46, census 7+1, assemble 9, couplings 4 (23 declared, 19 wires of 25, 4 intra), derive 575 oracle cases 0 mismatches. Item A holds: derive.run_windows_from_epochs refuses every wrong kind at the count end, refuses any Clock at the rate end and refuses a rate below 1, matching opt_steps_from_windows and opt_steps_from_backwards -- but the 575 oracle cases do not touch it, or opt_steps_from_backwards, or any of the five new Clock-rate refusals. Item B is REFUTED as a finding of this change: Plan really does declare no run_windows, but the pre-change body at HEAD~1 was already the inline multiply; plan.run_windows was introduced at 72a0917 and removed at d0c1223, five commits before HEAD, and HEAD~1's own docstring already records it -- HEAD's commit message re-claims a prior repair. Item C is REFUTED twice: no narrowing was made (tests/test_ownership.py is untouched and still skips all of src/spine/), and I demonstrated on a scratch copy that narrowing the skip to src/spine/derive.py leaves O11 GREEN with the inline multiply back in compose.py, because src/spine has no levers.py so `mine` is empty and the file is skipped a second line down. All five of item D were addressed and each repro reproduces. Item E holds and 03_WIRING.md is regenerated (render_wiring.py --check clean at HEAD~1, HEAD and the working tree). Item F is REFUTED: nothing in src/ or tools/ reads System.warnings, and System.refusals -- the alternative compose.py rejects on the ground that it 'would make a collapsed encoder abort the run' -- is equally unread, so that reasoning rests on a false premise. Four things in the diff are not on the list: the DEFERRED_ENTRY_POINTS recount in HEAD (checked mechanically, every number right), a 20-citation re-resolution sweep in compose.py and a 5-citation sweep plus a CAP.d_mask_dead_rows rewrite in assemble.py (both uncommitted, spot-checked against the cited symbols and correct), and one new false sentence about the deferrals.

findings.detail: The new named conversion exists and its guards are the ones claimed. `type(n_epochs) is not Epochs` refuses a bare int, a float, None, True and every one of the other five kinds plus a bare Clock; `isinstance(windows_in_epoch, Clock)` refuses a Clock at the rate end; `w < 1` refuses 0, -1 and 0.5. That is exactly the guard set opt_steps_from_windows and opt_steps_from_backwards carry, which I checked side by side. The value is right: run_windows_from_epochs(Epochs(3), 10) -> Windows(30), type Windows. The NO-FLOOR ruling in the docstring is honest -- RUN_EPOCHS=0 gives Windows(0), and train/api.py::startup_refusals does refuse `epochs < 1` with a sentence rather than clamping (I read the body). NARROWER THAN THE TASK ASSUMES IN ONE RESPECT ONLY: the 575 oracle cases do not exercise it. tests/test_derive.py replays eight tables (_phases, blowup_stale, bwt_of, cull_gate_open, curve_verdict, forgetting_of, lift_to, pin_tick) and its smoke block asserts flush_period, flush_period_windows, accum_due, opt_steps_from_windows, signature_width_bytes and pin_tick. run_windows_from_epochs appears nowhere in that file. That gap is filed in unfinished, not held against the function.

The claim that this change FOUND the plan.run_windows AttributeError is false, and the ledger should not record it as this round's discovery. The premise is true -- src/data/api.py::Plan declares (protocol, schedule, phase_bounds, per_area_draw, exposure, gates, counters) and has no run_windows field -- but `git show HEAD -- src/spine/compose.py` shows the two lines this change REMOVED were `from spine import units` / `return units.Windows(_windows_in_epoch(sysm) * int(sysm.configs['RUN'].epochs))`. plan.run_windows was INTRODUCED at 72a0917 (2026-08-30) and REPLACED by that inline multiply at d0c1223, five commits before HEAD, and HEAD~1's own _run_windows docstring already carries the paragraph 'THE BODY DID NOT DO WHAT THAT PARAGRAPH SAYS AND COULD NOT HAVE. It read `plan.run_windows`'. HEAD's commit message presents that as new work in the same paragraph that announces run_windows_from_epochs. What IS this change is the conversion, and it is correct.

Then: git log --oneline -S 'plan.run_windows' -- src/spine/compose.py  ;; got only 72a0917 (added). git log --oneline -S '_windows_in_epoch(sysm) * int(sysm.configs' -- src/spine/compose.py  ;; got d0c1223 (replaced it). git show HEAD~1:src/spine/compose.py | sed -n '2237p'  ;; the docstring already said it.

findings.detail: Second half of item B, and it holds. The replacement computes what the docstring says. `_run_windows` now calls derive.run_windows_from_epochs(units.Epochs(sysm.configs['RUN'].epochs), _windows_in_epoch(sysm)), and _windows_in_epoch returns max(1, len(sysm.segmentation.ids) // int(sysm.configs['LM'].ctx)) -- len(segmentation) // ctx, times epochs, measured on the token Segmentation and never on stream_bytes. (2) THE NARROWING WOULD NOT WORK. I copied the tree to a scratch dir, narrowed the skip to `if m.rel == os.path.join('src','spine','derive.py')`, put the inline multiply back into compose.py::_run_windows, and O11 STILL PASSED. findings.detail: The TRUNCATES-vs-FLOORS disagreement was real and the body is now truncation. Measured at HEAD~1: opt_steps_from_backwards(Backwards(-1), 4) -> Steps(-1) and Backwards(-5) -> Steps(-2). Live: Backwards(-1) -> Steps(0), Backwards(-4) -> Steps(-1), Backwards(-5) -> Steps(-1), Backwards(-8) -> Steps(-2). Positives are untouched -- -0,1,3 -> 0; 4,7 -> 1; 8 -> 2; 52 -> 13 -- so no live run's number moves, as claimed, and the integer form `n // k if n >= 0 else -((-n) // k)` avoids the float path the docstring rejects for exactness above 2**53. The repair matches the docstring's own rule ('a partial step is not a step, in either direction'). IT HAS AN UNDISCLOSED SIDE EFFECT ON THE ONE CALLER, filed in unfinished: opt/api.py::counters compares `due != taken`, and for a deficit of 1 to 3 backward passes with no steps taken the old floor gave Steps(-1) and raised while truncation gives Steps(0) and stays silent.

findings.detail: The seventh-kind escape was real and both closures work. On a scratch copy of HEAD~1 I added `class Ticks(Clock): KIND = "ticks"` with no __slots__: the module imported GREEN, Ticks was absent from CLOCK_KINDS, and `t.anything = 1` was accepted -- exactly the state the docstring describes. On the live module the same edit raises RuntimeError from Clock.__init_subclass__ naming the kind. All four arms of _verify_kind fire: no __slots__ -> refused; `__slots__ = ("gates",)` -> refused as a shadow; `__slots__ = ()` but absent from CLOCK_KINDS -> refused by the registry arm at import (proving the documented 'skipped during module execution, made up by _verify_gate_channel' path). OTHER DIRECTION CHECKED AND IT PASSES: a LEGITIMATE seventh kind -- `__slots__ = ()` and added to CLOCK_KINDS -- imports green and lands in CLOCK_KINDS, so the guard does not refuse a correct extension. The transitive `Clock.__subclasses__()` walk and the 'entry in CLOCK_KINDS that is not a kind' arm are both present and are new coverage the old `CLOCK_KINDS + (Clock,)` loop did not have.

Live + __slots__=() not registered: RuntimeError '... is a Clock kind that is not in CLOCK_KINDS'. Live + __slots__=() AND added to CLOCK_KINDS: 'IMPORTED GREEN; CLOCK_KINDS= [Steps, Flushes, Windows, Backwards, Epochs, Selections, Ticks]'.

findings.detail: Two documentation-only items in D, both measured and both accurate. (1) WEAKREF: at 30040f0~1, where Clock declared __slots__ = ('n',) and the six kinds declared none, weakref.ref(Windows(1)) succeeded; at HEAD~1 and today it raises "TypeError: cannot create weak reference to 'Windows' object". The docstring's claim that nothing needs one is also true: the only weakref in src/ is src/data/api.py:1451, `weakref.ref(areas, ...)` over an Areas. (2) THE __index__ COMMENT: `Windows(7) % 3` and `7 % Windows(3)` are both TypeError today and at HEAD~1, as are `//` and `*` in both directions, while range(), list indexing, slicing and hex() all work -- so the replacement comment is right where the old one ('so range(), slicing and % work') was wrong. One nuance the comment does not mention and which does not change its point: `'%d' % Windows(3)` succeeds, because that is str.__mod__ consuming __index__, not arithmetic modulo.

findings.detail: NOTHING READS System.warnings. `grep -rn '\.warnings' src/ tools/` finds only writes: compose.py:1926 (constructor), 2150 (the SIG 'collapsing' entry), 2185 (cadence_audit's lines) and 2267 (the missing-parameters() line). The one place outside compose that receives build()'s warnings, tools/render_wiring.py:49, unpacks them into a local and never uses it. So the SIG run-level failure still reaches an object graph and nothing else. WORSE, THE REASONING THAT PUT IT THERE IS FALSE: compose.py:2143 declines System.refusals on the ground that 'Appending to System.refusals would make a collapsed encoder abort the run', and System.refusals is equally unread -- it is written at 1957, 1958 and 2070 and read nowhere in src/ or tools/. Appending there would abort nothing. Both channels are write-only, which also means RUN.startup_refusals' 'RUN_EPOCHS=0: the loop would make no passes' does not stop the assembly today; run_windows_from_epochs would return Windows(0) and opt_steps_from_windows would floor the horizon to Steps(1). That last consequence is masked only because CAP.startup_refusals raises at compose.py:2070, seventeen lines before OPT.build -- which is the 'defect hidden behind an earlier stub' this same file names as the project's oldest shape.

unfinished.detail: src/opt/api.py:1496 computes `due = derive.opt_steps_from_backwards(st.n_backward - U.Backwards(base_bwd), divisor)` and raises when `due != taken`. The negative operand is reachable exactly here, as the derive docstring says. At accum=4 with a deficit of 1, 2 or 3 backward passes and no steps taken in this process, HEAD~1 gave due=Steps(-1) against taken=Steps(0) and RAISED; the tree today gives due=Steps(0) against Steps(0) and says nothing. Deficits of 4 or more still raise, and positives are untouched, so the window is narrow -- but it is the only window, and nothing else in the tree notices n_backward going backwards across a resume. The derive docstring's 'no live run's number moves' is true only of the positive side and does not disclose that the number it DOES move is the one the invariant reads. Repro: /tmp/.../w/old (HEAD~1) opt_steps_from_backwards(Backwards(-1),4) -> -1 steps; live tree -> 0 steps. WHAT TO ADD (owner: derive, one paragraph, no behaviour change): in src/spine/derive.py::opt_steps_from_backwards, after 'Positive counts are unaffected -- `//` and truncation agree for n >= 0 -- so no live run's number moves: the only reachable negative is the resume subtraction named above.' ADD: 'WHAT THAT COSTS AT THE ONE CALL SITE, SAID RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE FOUND. opt/api.py::counters raises on `due != taken`.
